normalization_notes: The supplied PGN had move-number display corruption after moves 42, 62, 85 and 89; the stored PGN normalizes them to 43, 63, 86 and 90 without changing SAN moves.
Fritz 'missed something' annotations are preserved as engine hints, not treated as independently verified best-move analysis.

observations.summary: Three consecutive flank-pawn tempi were spent before completing development or securing the king.
observations.training_rule: Before a non-central pawn push in the opening, count undeveloped minor pieces and ask whether the move creates a concrete threat.

observations.summary: Fritz marked the response to the discovered queen check as 'missed something'. Exact best play is not engine-verified here.
observations.training_rule: When in check, enumerate capture, block and king-move responses before selecting the most natural block.

observations.summary: A forcing check was inserted before completing the rook/bishop sequence, improving the tactical sequence.
observations.training_rule: Preserve the habit of looking for checks before routine recaptures or retreats.

observations.summary: Bb2 placed the bishop directly on the now-open b-file, allowing ...Rxb2 in one move.
observations.training_rule: Before placing a piece, scan enemy rook, bishop and queen rays through every newly vacated pawn file or diagonal.

observations.summary: The rook actively harvested g7 and kept practical pressure instead of retreating passively.
observations.training_rule: Keep active rook play as a strength, but pair it with an opponent-forcing-move scan.

observations.summary: The same b-file rook was allowed to enter b1 with check, forcing Nc1 and then winning that knight with ...Rxc1+.
observations.training_rule: Before every own move, perform an opponent CCT scan: checks first, then captures, then direct threats.

observations.summary: Fritz marked these moves as missed opportunities, but the exact tactical best moves were not independently verified.
observations.training_rule: Queue these positions for later engine-backed review instead of teaching an unverified answer.

observations.summary: The passed pawn was advanced with tempo and promoted with check, forcing the enemy rook to sacrifice itself.
After the rook trade, White had the elementary king-and-rook versus lone-king conversion but did not finish the mate over the remaining moves.
observations.training_rule: Cut the enemy king with the rook, bring your king up, shrink the box, then deliver the edge mate without repeated checking from distance.

primary_weaknesses: Long-range rook-ray blindness on open files
Insufficient opponent-check scan before committing an active move
strengths: Forcing checks and active tactical play
next_review: Engine-verify Fritz 'missed something' positions before converting them into answer-key tactics
